The cheapest new subscribers will come from the 140 you already have and the people already walking into your shop. Paid advertising can't compete with those on €300 a month.

## 1. Launch Christmas gift subscriptions this week
It's 19 November, so this is the most time-sensitive item. Sell 4-, 8- and 12-week gift boxes (€72 / €144 / €216) with a printed card the giver can hand over.
- Promote them at the till, in every box from this Saturday, and on Instagram and Google.
- People who receive a gift box are trying you for free. Put a "keep it going" offer in the last gift box. That is where most of the new subscribers will come from.

## 2. Referral programme
Offer existing subscribers a free box (€18) for each friend who signs up and stays at least 4 weeks. Give the friend €9 off their first box.
- That's €27 per new customer. If a subscriber stays about 6 months, they're worth roughly €470.
- Put a printed card with a short personal code in the box, so it lands on their kitchen table on Saturday morning.

## 3. Target the neighbours of current subscribers
Your bike already rides those streets, so every new subscriber there costs almost nothing extra to deliver.
- Put flyers through doors on streets where you already deliver: "Your neighbours get fresh sourdough every Saturday. Try a box."
- Add a sign or branded box to the cargo bike. It's a billboard that's out every Saturday morning.

## 4. Turn walk-in customers into subscribers
Ask regulars at the till: "Do you live within 3 km? We'll bring this to your door every Saturday." Make the first step small. A **3-week trial** with no commitment works better than asking for an open-ended subscription upfront.

## 5. Free channels
- **Google Business Profile:** add the bread box as a product, post photos weekly, and ask happy subscribers for reviews.
- **Local Facebook groups, neighbourhood WhatsApp groups and school parent groups:** one honest post from you, the owner, usually works better than an ad.

## Suggested €300 budget for this month
| Item | € |
|---|---|
| Printing: gift cards, referral cards, flyers | ~120 |
| Referral and trial discounts (most is only spent when someone signs up) | ~130 |
| Bike signage or a boosted Instagram post aimed within 3 km | ~50 |

## Two checks before you push hard
- **Delivery capacity:** how many more boxes can you bake and deliver on a Saturday morning before you need a second rider or route? Know that number before growth hits it.
- **Cancellations:** if you lose 5 subscribers a month, keeping them is as valuable as finding new ones. Offer a "pause" button for holidays instead of only "cancel", and ask everyone who leaves why.

If you tell me how your current subscribers found you, roughly how many cancel each month, and your Saturday capacity, I can turn this into a target and a week-by-week plan.
